canonical.name: The page proves the bounded-functional representation theorem concretely and leaves dual-space vocabulary to a final orientation-only remark.
The easy direction is separated from the representation theorem, and the norm equality item states explicitly that the q = infinity endpoint needs semifiniteness.

The finite-measure carrier is decomposed into the induced-measure, absolute-continuity, density-identification, and L^q-membership lemmas, because countable additivity and the L^q bound are real proof obligations.
The sigma-finite theorem and the arbitrary-measure 1 < p < infinity theorem are scaffolded separately, so the page does not smuggle a wider p = 1 claim into the headline statement.
The p = infinity case is recorded, not proved, and the batch does not fabricate a Banach-limit or Hahn-Banach construction locally.
The examples page keeps only the design's concrete norms, sequence-space instance, quotient warning, and endpoint boundary witnesses; it does not pad with extra abstract false statements.
